findings.evidence:
Planner unconditionally appends an extra `_tidb_commit_ts` column into every `DataSource` schema/names: `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:4648`-`pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:4658`.
Planner then hard-blocks any SQL column reference by *name* `_tidb_commit_ts` in SELECT/SET-OPR/UPDATE/DELETE: `pkg/planner/core/preprocess.go:452`-`pkg/planner/core/preprocess.go:457`.
DML planning also removes/prunes by *name* (not by column ID):
- UPDATE freezes output columns then deletes any output named `_tidb_commit_ts`: `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:5497`-`pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:5502`.
- DELETE column pruning always clears any column named `_tidb_commit_ts`: `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:5261`-`pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:5266`.
NATURAL JOIN ignores `_tidb_commit_ts` by name when computing common columns: `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:787`-`pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:806`.
findings.fix:
If `_tidb_commit_ts` is intended to be a reserved pseudo/hidden column name, enforce it at DDL time (CREATE/ALTER COLUMN name checks) so user tables can’t contain a real column with that name.
Additionally (defense-in-depth), prefer filtering/removing by column ID (`model.ExtraCommitTSID`) instead of `FieldName.ColName` where feasible (e.g., in the UPDATE projection cleanup), and return a more appropriate user-facing error class/code than `plannererrors.ErrInternal` for explicit usage attempts.
findings.impact: Compatibility/SQL semantics risk: any existing user schema that already has a real column named `_tidb_commit_ts` will become effectively unusable in core DML/queries (SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE) because the planner rejects the column name outright and/or prunes it by name. Even without explicit reference, injecting an internal column with the same name into every `DataSource` can create duplicate-name edge cases that are then “handled” by ad-hoc name-based ignores/prunes (NATURAL JOIN, DELETE pruning, UPDATE column freezing).
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked history up to `upstream/master` and found no evidence of a follow-up fix that removes these name-based guards or moves the reservation to DDL-level enforcement (e.g., `git grep` on `upstream/master` still shows the `ExtraCommitTSName` preprocessor guard and planner-side name-based removal).
findings.verify:
1) On this commit, create a table with a real column named `_tidb_commit_ts` (if DDL allows), then run `SELECT _tidb_commit_ts FROM t`, `UPDATE t SET _tidb_commit_ts=...`, and `DELETE ... WHERE _tidb_commit_ts ...` and confirm planner errors/pruning behavior.
2) After implementing the fix, verify either: (a) DDL rejects such a column name consistently, or (b) user-defined `_tidb_commit_ts` behaves normally while only the pseudo-column is blocked/hidden.
3) Re-check NATURAL JOIN / `USING` / `SELECT *` behavior for tables around this reserved name.
findings.what: `_tidb_commit_ts` is treated as a globally reserved pseudo column name in planner/executor prep code via name-based blocking and pruning, but the reservation is enforced primarily at query-planning time (and by name), not by column ID or DDL-level prevention. This can break backward compatibility for any user tables that legitimately have a real column named `_tidb_commit_ts` (queries error out or the column is silently pruned/ignored).
